physical.mounting-hardware: 2 M5 screws and 2 M5 cage nuts (Packaging); Rev 01 lists 2 10/32 and 2 12/24 screws and 2 cage nuts (Special Notes)

configs.description: The hook as StarTech.com ships CMHOOKMW.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the datasheet and the drawing state no cable capacity, no fill and no cable count.
gaps.wanted: a cable capacity table, or a stated fill, for the hook

gaps.note: the datasheet says the bracket's two sets of mounting holes let the ring face inward or outward. The plate drawn is one leg, with the loop standing out of the rail; the other leg (15.0 wide, with its own two slots 7.0 from its edge) and the loop's position when it is bolted through, facing along the rail, are not drawn, and the format has no key that turns a part on its rail into a second facing.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the hook bolted through its other leg, and a placement key that selects the facing

gaps.note: the 14.5 mm opening in the side wall of the loop beside the plate is the "wide front opening for quick cable insertion", drawn in the relief; the format's ring `slit` is a range of height along a leg and cannot state a gap along a side wall, so the ring is declared with its clear opening and no slit.
gaps.wanted: a format key for a gap in a ring's side wall, or a route kit that reads the opening

gaps.note: the plan dimensions 15.0 between the plate and the loop and the isometric draws a bend there; no view says how the bracket is bent, so a straight neck 8.5 mm across and the loop's 25.5 high joins them (estimated).
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned view of the bracket from above, showing the bend
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - the material (steel), colour, the standard (EIA RS310-D) and the racks it fits are the datasheet's. Its box is stated twice: "Rev 01 of this product includes ... 2 10/32 screws, 2 12/24 screws, 2 24/24 cage nuts" under Special Notes and "2 M5 screws, 2 M5 cage nuts" under Packaging; both are in `mounting-hardware`.

capacity.note: no document states a cable capacity: the datasheet and the drawing are silent, so none is stated and a gap says so.

chassis.note: estimated - 111.0 x 70.1 x 117.0. The 111.0 is the drawing's overall extent across the rail (the 55.0 plate and the 64.0 loop, 8.5 mm of them overlapping), the 70.1 the plate's height, and the 117.0 the loop's 102.0 out of a neck 15.0 from the plate, which is how the plan reads: 15.0 and 102.0 dimensioned side by side. The datasheet's "Length 4.0 in" is the loop's 102.0 alone, so the depth is 15 mm more than the datasheet says; whether the 15.0 is a joggle between the plate and the loop is read, not stated (the device's `joggle` gap).

color.note: estimated - "Color: Black". The drawing is line work, so the shades are this library's render of black steel, the ring a little lighter than the plate.

front.note: drawing - the side view: the plate with its 45 degree cuts and two slots, and the loop's far end, 25.5 high and 64 wide, on its tab.

hand.note: drawing - the front view draws the loop on the right of the plate, 8.5 mm of it overlapping the plate's tab. The drawing does not say which rail it is drawn for. It is drawn as that view draws it, the plate on the left, which is how a part stands on the left rail (as `fs/cmv-5u3w` is drawn); on the right rail the kit turns it end over end (kit/rack/solids.js and route.js mirror a narrow rack-face part there).

left.note: drawing - the front view of the drawing: the plate, the neck and the loop's 25.5 high band standing out of it. The right is the same, turned round.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S OWN DRAWING. StarTech.com publishes CMHOOKMW_Diagram.pdf (third angle projection, millimetres, 6/15/2022): a plan, a front view, a side view and an isometric, with the dimensions 15.0, 102.0, 111.0, 64.0, 14.5, 85.5, 70.1, 44.5, 25.5, 55.0, 32.7, 11.2, 7.0, "45 deg" and "2-phi6.0x10.0". The datasheet (cmhookmw_datasheet.pdf) lists "Product Length 4.0 in [10.2 cm]", "Product Width 2.8 in [70.1 mm]" and "Product Height 4.4 in [11.1 cm]": the 102, the plate's 70.1 and the 111.0 across the bracket and the loop. The drawing's views are read as the bracket seen along the rail (the 55 mm leg with the ring end on), across it, and from above.

mount.note: drawing - `rack-face`. The datasheet says the hook "mounts vertically to 2-post and 4-post racks and supports both 10-inch and 19-inch rack systems" and that its "right-angled mounting bracket with 2 sets of mounting holes" lets the ring face inward or outward. The plate drawn here is the 55 mm leg, flat on the face of one rail with its two slots 44.5 apart, the spacing of two rack holes a unit apart. It is narrower than the opening, so a lab places it with a `side` (docs/vertical-cable-managers-design.md section 3.4).

rear.note: drawing - the back of the plate, the face that lies on the rail, mirrored, with its two slots and the loop's closed end showing past it. The 45 degree cuts are drawn as two steps in 2D.

rings.note: estimated - the loop is the ring: a component with a `ring` guide whose opening is the 57.6 by 95.6 left inside a 3.2 wall (see its contract), cables passing up and down the rail through it.

ru.note: datasheet - "U Height 1.5U". `chassis.ru` is a number and the rack kit counts half units (`unitsOf` rounds a stated `ru` up to the next half), so the part states `ru: 1.5` as its maker does and claims a unit and a half on its rail. The plate is 70.1 mm high, 1.58 U, and its two slots are 44.5 apart, one unit's hole pitch. `chassis.height` is the 70.1 the drawing gives. The format is not changed.

thickness.note: estimated - no CMHOOKMW document states a gauge. 2.3 mm, the maker's CMHOOK1U plate, is taken.

top.note: drawing - an elevation, rear at the top: the plate 2.3 thick, the neck to the loop, and the loop's outline, a wall 3.2 mm thick (estimated), its side wall beside the plate open for 14.5 mm. The bottom is the same.
